title: DO NOT START BEFORE 28 NOV 2026 - Policy deadline check, Nov-Dec 2026: BIS affiliates-rule suspension, China's 10 Nov and 27 Nov suspensions, US-China truce extension, and other dated trade measures
why_it_matters: Many 2025-26 chip trade measures are suspended, not repealed, and expire within weeks (CLM-0366): the BIS affiliates rule (REG-0008) is due to return on 10 Nov 2026 unless BIS publishes an extension (CLM-0306, CLM-2258); China's suspensions under MOFCOM Announcement 2025 No. 70 (REG-0058, REG-0059, REG-0029) end 10 Nov 2026 and No. 72 (REG-0028) on 27 Nov 2026 (CLM-1385, CLM-1396); China's UEL and export-control-list suspensions run 'for another year' from 10 Nov 2025 (CLM-1409, CLM-1410); the US Treasury says the Busan truce is extended to 10 Jan 2027 (CLM-2257). The regulations database and atlas must state what is actually in force, with dates.
questions: Did BIS publish a Federal Register notice extending (or ending) the suspension of the Entity List affiliates rule (90 FR 47201), and what is its new end date?
Did MOFCOM/GACC extend, lapse or replace the suspension in Announcement 2025 No. 70 (rare earths, superhard materials, lithium battery/graphite, rare-earth technology controls) after 10 Nov 2026?
Did MOFCOM extend or let lapse the suspension of paragraph 2 of Announcement 2024 No. 46 (US-specific gallium, germanium, antimony and superhard materials ban) after 27 Nov 2026?
What happened to China's suspended Unreliable Entity List and export-control-list measures against US firms (MOFCOM 2025 Nos. 7, 13 and related) when their one-year suspension ended?
What official text (White House fact sheet, MOFCOM statement, Treasury readout) documents the extension of the US-China arrangement to 10 Jan 2027, and which measures does it cover?
Has a second-phase Section 232 semiconductor proclamation been issued (CLM-0322), and did the polysilicon Section 232 import adjustment start on 4 Dec 2026 as scheduled?
What is the status at the time of research of the foundry/OSAT due-diligence compliance deadline (31 Dec 2026, REG-0045) and the 48D construction-start deadline (31 Dec 2026, REG-0014)?
For each measure, which regulation records (REG-0005, REG-0008, REG-0014, REG-0028, REG-0029, REG-0045, REG-0057, REG-0058, REG-0059, REG-0068) need a status change, with the dated legal source?
subquestions: Record each status as a new dated claim; propose patches for regulation status/status_as_of with the legal source; do not edit old claims.
primary_sources: Federal Register (federalregister.gov API) BIS rules on 15 CFR 744 (affiliates rule, 90 FR 47201 and its suspension)
MOFCOM announcements (mofcom.gov.cn, 公告 2025 No. 70, No. 72; 2024 No. 46) and GACC joint announcements
MOFCOM Unreliable Entity List working mechanism notices
White House fact sheets and US Treasury/USTR readouts on the US-China arrangement
Federal Register presidential documents (Section 232 proclamations)
IRS/Treasury guidance on 26 U.S.C. 48D
secondary_sources: Crowell & Moring, Miller & Chevalier, Akin export-control alerts (to locate the legal texts)
entities: Ministry of Commerce of the PRC
General Administration of Customs of the PRC
open_questions: Timing: the orchestrator must not dispatch before 28 Nov 2026 (after both China deadlines). irs has no start-date field, so the date is in the title.
A follow-up pass after 10 Jan 2027 is the separate unit 'Policy deadline check, Jan 2027'.
Cross-check RU-0027 (Section 232/301 tariffs) if it has run; this unit records only the dated status changes.

title: DO NOT START BEFORE 11 JAN 2027 - Policy deadline check, Jan 2027: end of the extended US-China truce and year-end 2026 US deadlines
why_it_matters: The US-China arrangement was extended to 10 Jan 2027 (CLM-2257) and two US deadlines fall on 31 Dec 2026 (48D construction start, foundry due-diligence compliance). Status of the suspended measures changes again after these dates.
questions: What happened to the US-China arrangement on or after 10 Jan 2027 (renewed, replaced, lapsed), per official texts?
Which US and Chinese suspended measures (affiliates rule; MOFCOM 2025 No. 70 and 2024 No. 46 suspensions; UEL listings) came back into force or were extended?
Was the 48D construction-start deadline extended by legislation, and did the foundry due-diligence compliance date take effect or move?
Which regulation records need a status update as of the research date?
primary_sources: Federal Register (BIS, Treasury/IRS)
MOFCOM and GACC announcements
White House and USTR statements
congress.gov (48D bills)
open_questions: Timing: do not dispatch before 11 Jan 2027.

title: Workflow: inside the fab from wafer start to wafer out (lot release, routing, dispatching, AMHS, metrology sampling, holds and rework, cycle time per mask layer, WIP and utilisation)
why_it_matters: The atlas traces work between firms (order-to-delivery RU-0164, tape-out RU-0162, yield excursions RU-0166) but not the core operating workflow inside a fab, which sets lead times, capacity and cost. Public operations literature exists (e.g. the Berkeley CSM competitive semiconductor manufacturing benchmarks report cycle time per mask layer; industry press cites about 1-1.5 days per layer) but none is in the atlas.
questions: How does a lot move through a fab: release/wafer start, process route (hundreds of steps), dispatching rules, batching (furnaces, wet benches), automated material handling (FOUPs, overhead hoist transport)?
What is fab cycle time (days per mask layer, total days for mature vs leading-edge flows), and how does it rise with utilisation (Little's Law, operating curves)?
Which metrology and inspection steps are sampled, and how are lots held, reworked or scrapped?
Who makes which decisions (manufacturing, process, equipment and industrial engineers; operators/technicians) and what is automated versus manual?
What do public benchmarks (Berkeley CSM reports, company disclosures of cycle time or 'super hot runs') say about differences between fabs?
Who supplies the dispatching/scheduling and AMHS systems (link RU-0035) and how concentrated is supply (Daifuku, Murata Machinery, Applied SmartFactory)?
primary_sources: UC Berkeley Competitive Semiconductor Manufacturing (CSM) reports (ieor.berkeley.edu)
SEMI standards E10 (equipment reliability), E79 (productivity), E90/E87 (substrate and carrier tracking)
Daifuku and Murata Machinery annual reports (cleanroom AMHS segments)
TSMC, GlobalFoundries, Micron annual reports/20-F (cycle-time, utilisation and capacity disclosures)
IEEE Transactions on Semiconductor Manufacturing (operations papers)
open_questions: Brief gap check (gap-W1R2-6ad7): a Berkeley CSM-31 report with 'cycle time per mask layer' and a SemiEngineering 'Battling Fab Cycle Times' article (2017) exist; researcher must open and quote them.

title: Adjacent: electricity, grid and power equipment as a constraint on AI data centres and chip fabs (2024-2030)
why_it_matters: Whether silicon or power is the binding constraint on AI build-out is an open contradiction (CON-0023; CLM-0772 vs IEA CLM-0815). Grid connection queues, transformer and gas-turbine lead times and utility tariffs decide how many accelerators can be deployed, and fabs themselves need firm power (Taiwan, Yongin, Arizona). The adjacent dimension has no claims yet.
questions: How much electricity do data centres and AI data centres use now and in official projections (IEA Energy and AI, US DOE/LBNL, EPRI), and what share is AI accelerators?
How long are grid interconnection and large-load connection queues in the main AI regions (US ISOs, Ireland, Netherlands, Japan, Taiwan), per LBNL 'Queued Up' and regulators?
What are lead times and supply constraints for large power transformers, switchgear and gas turbines (DOE, NERC, manufacturer disclosures), and are they delaying AI capacity?
Which hyperscaler or chip-company disclosures say power, not chips, limits deployment (10-K risk factors, earnings calls)?
What firm-power arrangements do chip fabs and clusters rely on (Taipower supply plans, Korea Yongin cluster power plan, APS/SRP contracts), and what shortfalls are reported?
Which semiconductor segments sell into the power build-out (power discretes, SiC/GaN, grid-edge chips), and how large is that demand?
primary_sources: IEA 'Energy and AI' (latest edition)
LBNL 'Queued Up: 2025 Edition' (Dec 2025) and LBNL US data-center energy report
NERC Long-Term Reliability Assessment
US DOE large power transformer supply-chain assessment
FERC large-load interconnection proceedings
Taipower and Taiwan MOEA power supply plans; Korea MOTIE Yongin cluster plan
Hyperscaler 10-K risk factors (Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta)
open_questions: Brief gap check (gap-W1R2-6ad7): LBNL 'Queued Up: 2025 Edition' (Dec 2025, data to end-2024) confirmed to exist. Feeds RU-0206 (AI capex risk) and RU-0010 (scope).
Electricity tariffs for specific fabs stay in RU-0277.

title: Evidence upgrade: re-source tier-3-only metric claims and analyst figures to the original publisher (Omdia, Counterpoint, TrendForce, UBS/JPMorgan, ITRI, company releases)
why_it_matters: 56 metric claims (fact/estimate/reported) rest only on tier-3 mirrors: CoWoS capacity estimates via TechFlow/Tiger Brokers (CLM-1263, CLM-1591-1594), Omdia market totals via MacTech (CLM-0719-0723, CLM-1254), Counterpoint DRAM shares via Tiger Brokers/Huawei Central (CLM-1258-1261), Micron HBM via MarketBeat (CLM-0785/0786), ITRI packaging output via reposts (CLM-1108/1109), Naura revenue via Tiger Brokers (CLM-1955), Taipower tariff via Taipei Times (CLM-2143). They feed open contradictions CON-0022 and CON-0052 (CoWoS capacity). Confidence cannot rise until the original document is cited.
questions: Where the original differs from the mirror (value, period, definition), what is the correct figure? Record a contradiction if they disagree.
For analyst capacity estimates with no public original (UBS, JPMorgan CoWoS figures), what is the earliest traceable publication and its stated methodology?
Which of these figures can be replaced with a company-disclosed or official figure (e.g. Micron 8-K exhibits for HBM revenue, Naura SZSE annual report, Taipower tariff tables, ITRI/IEK releases)?
primary_sources: Original press releases on omdia.tech.informa.com, counterpointresearch.com, trendforce.com, yolegroup.com
SEC EDGAR 8-K exhibits (Micron, Amkor)
SZSE/cninfo annual reports (Naura)
Taipower rate tables (taipower.com.tw)
ITRI/IEK press releases (itri.org.tw)
TSMC MOPS filings
open_questions: Record re-sourced figures as new claims citing the original; mention the superseded claim id in notes so fact-checkers can mark the old one. Do not edit old claims.
List computed by gap-W1R2-6ad7 on 2026-10-01: fact/estimate/reported_claim claims with a metric whose sources are all tier 3.
